question: Should OpenClaw accept Vault as a bundled exec SecretRef provider after fixing the plugin-boundary violation, and should generic SecretRef target lookup become a public SDK/setup seam or remain core-owned?
rationale: Automation can identify the boundary break, but maintainers must choose the permanent ownership shape for generic target discovery and approve the bundled resolver that receives Vault credentials and reads over the network.

options.title: Approve bundled Vault with a narrow seam
options.body: Add or reuse a focused public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` setup seam for SecretRef target lookup, remove the core-source imports from the plugin, then require secops/admin approval on the exact head.

options.title: Narrow the Vault CLI for now
options.body: Drop the generic `--target` expansion from the plugin and keep only provider-key setup until a public target registry seam is designed.

options.title: Move Vault outside core
options.body: Pause this bundled plugin and route Vault to ClawHub or a separately owned official plugin package if maintainers do not want this resolver in the core distribution.

recommendation.title: Approve bundled Vault with a narrow seam
recommendation.body: Add or reuse a focused public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` setup seam for SecretRef target lookup, remove the core-source imports from the plugin, then require secops/admin approval on the exact head.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the exec SecretRef trust boundary and setup/apply behavior he introduced and maintained.
